The segment of this campaign, `20261027-com260-m1b`, runs from the first `te-poc` run's `BE_MVP:01` line (log line 85,536) to the end of the log as read (line 94,579; 17:53 to 18:02 UTC). For each of the six runs it holds Fedora's shutdown through `systemd-kexec.service`, the kexec handoff, the shim line, and the monitor's lines through the run's terminal marker, `BE_MVP:14 SHUTDOWN type=0 reason=0` four times (`te-poc`, three GCC and one Clang), `BE_MVP:FAIL gstage` once (`reader-write`) and `BE_MVP:FAIL guest-page-fault` once (`no-inject`, hart 0's one FAIL and DETAIL pair, after both domains' `MVPINIT 07 CHANNEL` lines, and nothing from a domain hart); then, after each `k3ctl reset`, two NUL bytes and the boot ROM's terse lines (`sys: 0x10000200`, `try sd...`, `bm:3`, `ERROR: CMD8`, `ERROR: sd f! l:90`, `bm:4`, `nor m:0xc8 d:0x6017`, `j...`), `U-Boot SPL 2022.10 (May 21 2026 - 07:43:32 +0000)` with its DDR line (MT62F1G32D2DS, 4096MB, 6400MT/s), `U-Boot 2022.10 (May 21 2026 - 07:43:32 +0000), Build: jenkins-BSP-build-bsp-deb-395` with its device probes, `Starting kernel ...`, and Fedora Linux 45 (Server) with kernel `7.3.0-65.1.riscv64.omni.fc45.riscv64` to its login prompt: six such reboots, each legible and complete. No line with `OpenSBI`, `Platform Name`, `Domain0`, `PMP`, `Firmware Base`, or `Runtime SBI` appears in the segment, as in M0's campaign (mvp/README.md open item 40): the firmware is identified only by Fedora's log, `SBI implementation ID=0x1 Version=0x10006`, which the preflight records. Earlier in the same log are the first M1 campaign (`20261027-com260`, 09:32 to 09:41 UTC), whose `no-inject` run ended in both domain harts' own FAIL and DETAIL lines and a halt with no further output until the `k3ctl reset` at 17:45 UTC that preceded this campaign's preflight, and, between that reset and this segment, the preflight, two `two-guests` load checks, three unplanned `two-guests` kexec runs with this campaign's images (made by an invocation without `SCENARIO=te-poc`, set aside and not part of this record), and the two `te-poc` load checks.
